title: Cannot reinstall Thunderbird
creator: bobh123usa
content:
I have run Thunderbird for many years. My PC is Windows 11. A couple of days ago the computer did not boot up. I took it to the Geek Squad. They reported that the OS was corrupted, so they reinstalled the operating system. The computer now boots up, but a casualty is that several applications or other items have to be reinstalled or modified. Many apps worked fine even after the OS reinstallation.

When I tried to run T-bird, I got an error of “Thunderbird is already running, but is not responding. The old Thunderbird process must be closed to open a new window.”

I closed Thunderbird and removed T-bird from the task manager and tried to run T-bird again. Same error.

I read that this is because there is a parent.lock file in the appdata\roaming\Thunderbird\profiles folder, and it should be deleted. I closed Thunderbird and removed T-bird from the task manager. I then renamed the parent.lock files as parent.lockold.

I tried running T-bird again, but got the same error.

I uninstalled T-bird. I then reinstalled T-bird.

I tried running T-bird and got the same error. I closed Thunderbird and removed T-bird from the task manager. I then searched for all parent.lock files on my c: drive, and renamed them parent.lockold. I ran T-bird and got to the initial login screen I went through creating a new account and signed out. I then edited the profiles.ini file to use a default profile on the NAS. I ran T-bird and got to the screen asking which profile I wanted to run. I selected the one on the NAS. T-bird opened. It looked OK. I closed it. I then tried to open it again, and got the same error.

I just tried again. I made sure T-bird was not shown as running in task manager. I renamed all parent.lock files as parent.lockold. I get the same message.

There must be some way to get a clear restart of T-bird. How can I absolutely start with a clean slate with T-bird, so that I can reinstall it and then specify using the default profile on the NAS? Is there better solution?

I have the version of T-bird that is downloaded from the website today. Since I can't open T-bird, I can't firm which version it is. I think I recall it was 140.xxxx.

Thanks.

title: What TB version is now recommended, V.159 or V.160?
creator: tsbtonon
content:
A couple weeks ago my TB V.159 crashed and I was prompted to create a new profile which I did, but I made the mistake to set the new profile as a POP account. This profile loaded and I found that a few archived subfolders were missing. Also, I'm not able even now to find a "sent" subdirectory that stores my newly sent messages and so I don't know what's happening to them. In other words, my TB V.159 is not usable.

My plan is to delete my current TB software, but before doing that, (in my Windows 11 computer), I'll change my AppData\[redacted]\Roaming\Thunderbird subfolder to AppData\[redacted]\Roaming\OLDTunderbirdOLD. This change will ensure that I don't lose any user profiles in the Thunderbird subdirectory by accident during uninstall and re-install.

I'll then download TB, and I'm inclined to download V.160 if the consensus here is favorable, and then build another user profile set as IMAP because under no circumstances do I ever want TB to delete data on my Network Solutions Internet Host server.

A final question, how do I find the password I'm currently using for TB to download my email from Network Solutions?

Many thanks for the help. Tom
